entries.subject: 2025 occultation and photometric shape model
entries.finding: The selected model uses inferred semiaxes 240±40, 180±30 and 143±7 km under homogeneous surface brightness. These correlated uncertainties do not define independent shape extremes. Numerical facts and an authored ellipsoid are used; the article and workbook are not relicensed.

entries.subject: Occultation Source Data workbook event label
entries.finding: The retained workbook review found a 2023-04-16 label conflicting with 2021 event/year data; the label is not used as an epoch. Article CC BY-NC-ND terms do not establish permission for adapted graphics.
entries.revisitWhen: The source resolves the event-label discrepancy and any proposed derivative has applicable reuse terms.

entries.subject: Haumea-aligned pole transformation
entries.finding: The Haumea-aligned pole has not been correctly transformed into the display frame. The occultation aspect angle is not inertial declination, so orientation and phase remain illustrative.
entries.revisitWhen: A documented inertial transformation and phase convention qualify the physical orientation.

entries.subject: Retained JPL number 110 Haumea system solution
entries.finding: The fixed-epoch placement uses the older 2005–2008 observation-based JPL solution. Its reported 900 km uncertainty is at 2025-Jan-01 and is not a 2026 bound; runtime extrapolation is disabled.

entries.subject: 2024 non-Keplerian Haumea satellite orbit
entries.finding: The newer interacting-satellite study was identified, but the current package retains JPL number 110. No implementation or current-epoch validation of the newer orbit is claimed.
entries.revisitWhen: The interacting solution is acquired with its frame, epoch and uncertainty and independently checked for the application epoch.

entries.subject: Occultation and disk photometry as mapped imagery
entries.finding: The examined observations constrain an inferred shape and integrated brightness. They do not supply a resolved photographic or composition texture; the current surface is unmapped.
entries.revisitWhen: A spatially resolved Hiʻiaka observation with controlled surface coordinates is available.
